calls.reason: Pre-post studies show weak citation support in generative search (about 51.5% recall) and RARR reporting major headroom, but 'no reason to think' is a judgement and two papers cannot map the whole field.

The claim is expressed as doubt, not a firm forecast. The only pre-deadline evidence is one July 2026 ARC benchmark gap, and the strongest progress (GPT-6 Astra) was reported after the deadline with no agreed AGI test.
Stack Overflow surveys show developer favourability toward AI staying a majority, 60% in 2025 and 62% in 2026, despite a fall from 72% and frustration with almost-right code.
OpenAI's projected $200M for 2023 fits the rumour, but Bloomberg put 2022 industry revenue near $40B, hardware included. No comparable aggregate figure or link to valuation assumptions settles it.

HEPI's survey supports continued undergraduate use (94%), but the open-source shift was hedged and has no deadline. The only product evidence is institution-provided ChatGPT and Copilot, not student migration.
Schumer's June 2023 speech puts innovation first and sets a months-long timeline, but the packet names no consumer-protection measure that was delayed because of pressure to speed development.
